test_title: PYST 30: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 21 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which district became the first in India to meet its entire power demand through solar energy, as of 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Diu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diu**, a district in the Union Territory of Daman and Diu, became the **first district in India to meet its entire power demand through solar energy**.
 
• The district achieved this milestone by generating enough **solar power** to meet the electricity needs of its population.
 
• Diu has installed a **9 MW solar power plant** and rooftop solar plants, which together generate sufficient power to meet the district’s energy needs.
 
• Through this initiative, Diu has significantly reduced its dependency on conventional power sources and has become a model for adopting **clean and renewable energy solutions**.
 
• This achievement was made possible due to the **government’s efforts to promote renewable energy**, in line with India’s commitment to reducing carbon emissions and combating climate change.
 
• The project has also helped the local population by bringing down electricity tariffs and providing a more **stable and sustainable power supply**.
 
• Diu’s transition to solar energy serves as an example of how small regions can take significant steps towards a **clean energy future** and contribute to environmental sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Diu:**

 
 
• Diu is a small district in the Union Territory of **Daman and Diu**, located on the western coast of India.
 
• It is known for its scenic beaches, historic forts, and Portuguese colonial architecture.
 
 
 
• **Solar Energy in India:**
 
 
• India is one of the world’s leading countries in **solar energy generation**, with ambitious targets under the **National Solar Mission**.
 
• As of 2023, India aims to achieve a capacity of **280 GW of solar power** by 2030.
 
• **Key initiatives** to promote solar energy include rooftop solar programs, solar parks, and subsidies for solar installations.
 
 
 
• **Other Districts Promoting Solar Energy:**
 
 
• **Leh:** Located in Ladakh, Leh is also making significant progress in harnessing solar and wind energy due to its high altitude and abundant sunlight.
 
• **Kavaratti:** The capital of Lakshadweep is working to integrate renewable energy sources into its power grid, but it has not yet achieved complete reliance on solar energy.
 
• **Silvassa:** The capital of Dadra and Nagar Haveli has implemented some solar energy initiatives, but it still relies on conventional power sources.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India’s Renewable Energy Goals:**

 
 
• India is committed to achieving **net-zero carbon emissions by 2070**, as announced at the COP26 Climate Summit.
 
• The country has set a target of **500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity** by 2030.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Solar Energy:**
 
 
• Solar energy is a **clean, renewable, and sustainable source of power** that reduces dependence on fossil fuels.
 
• It helps in reducing **greenhouse gas emissions** and combating climate change.
 
• Solar energy systems have lower operational costs and can provide **energy security** to remote areas.
